return.plan:
Land the four-row failure-to-form table and the exemption-clause ban in one new path-scoped rule page, point the two existing authoring pages at it, and guard every row of the table cell by cell so an inversion cannot stay green. Three production files and one suite file change.

## 1. The home: a new `.claude/rules/authoring.md`

Create it with exactly this content (it is the page INC-1 landed and its reviewer accepted word for word against criteria 1, 2 and 3; recover it verbatim with `git show origin/claude/authoring-rule-form-matching-c5ygkt--INC-1:.claude/rules/authoring.md`):

```
---
paths:
  - "skills/**"
  - "agents/**"
---
# The form of a rule

A rule fails in a particular way, and the form that repairs it follows from
that way and not from taste. The rows below come from measured head-to-head
wording tests (obra/superpowers, `skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md`, "Match the
Form to the Failure"), so a row changes when a new measurement says so.

Find the failure your rule prevents, then write it in the form that column
names.

| Failure class | Form that works | Form that fails | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A rule skipped under pressure | A prohibition that carries its price and quotes, verbatim, the rationalisation it counters | An unpriced reminder to keep the rule in mind | Under pressure an agent trades away a rule whose cost of skipping is unnamed, and an unquoted excuse stays available. |
| A wrong output shape | A recipe that states what the output is | A list of prohibitions | A ban names what not to emit and leaves the shape unstated, which measured worse than no guidance at all. |
| An omitted required element | A required slot in the schema or the template | Prose in the body asking for the element | A slot makes the omission visible in the artefact, while prose is satisfied by an agent that believes it complied. |
| Behaviour that depends on a condition | A rule keyed to an observable predicate | A judgement call, or an exemption bolted onto the general rule | A predicate the agent can evaluate decides both branches, and a judgement call decides neither. |

Never patch a working rule with an exemption clause. Re-cut the rule on an
observable predicate instead, and state each branch on its own: one appended
exemption measured a working rule down from consistent to noisy.

This page stays in this checkout rather than in the shipped brief because it
binds whoever writes a page here, not an agent at run time.
```

The wording is load-bearing for the suite: the guards read the second and third cell of each row, so any reword of a cell has to keep that row's markers (listed in the test plan) in the winning cell and out of the failing cell.

Why this file and this frontmatter. `.claude/rules/` exists only in this checkout, which is what the rule needs: it binds whoever edits a page here, not an agent at run time. Every page there must carry `paths:` frontmatter and every pattern must match tracked files — `test-repo.sh` already checks both (its "no repository-local rule reaches an agent" section, at test-repo.sh:60-121) — and the list form of `paths:` used above is accepted by that parser, which reads an inline value and then any `-` list items beneath. `skills/**` and `agents/**` are the two audiences, and both match tracked files, so the page loads for whoever opens a skill page or an agent page and for nobody else.

## 2. The two pointers

- `skills/CLAUDE.md`, after the last paragraph of "Where a rule belongs" (the paragraph ending "...even when it reads like a detail."), one sentence and nothing more: `This section decides where a rule lives; `.claude/rules/authoring.md` decides what form it takes.` INC-1's first review round rejected a longer version of this sentence that also restated why the page is not in the shipped brief; keep it to the one clause.
- `.claude/rules/agents.md`, after the paragraph ending "A rule that stands in both drifts." (line 73) and before "The one exception opens every page:", one sentence: `The form a rule on an agent page takes is decided by `.claude/rules/authoring.md`.` (INC-1 wrote "is `.claude/rules/authoring.md`", which equates a form with a path; its reviewer flagged the wording twice as an observation.)

Neither pointer may restate the table, the ban or the page's placement rationale: criterion 4 and the repository's own one-home rule (`skills/CLAUDE.md`, "Interface and inside": "Describe each thing once. Where another page owns a rule, point at the owner instead of restating it") forbid it, and the suite pins it with two ownership cases.

## 3. The suite

One new section at the end of `test-repo.sh`, inserted immediately before the closing `echo` / `if [ "$failed" -eq 0 ]` summary block, headed `echo "=== a rule's form is picked by the failure it prevents"`. Thirteen cases, spelled out in the test plan.

The decision this increment turns on. INC-1 wrote three of its four row cases as `grep -i '<failure class>' file | grep -qi '<winning form>'`. A Markdown table row is one physical line carrying the failure class, the winning form and the failing form at once, so swapping the winning and failing cells leaves every word on that line and the grep still passes — the table would then pair each failure class with the form measured to lose, with the suite green. So every row case parses the table into cells and asserts on the cell, never on the line: the row's markers must all appear in cell 2 (the form that works) and none of them may appear in cell 3 (the form that fails). The second half is what makes the case an inversion guard rather than a presence check.

A fifth column-level hole comes with it: if the two column headers are swapped instead of the cells, all four rows invert at once while every cell keeps its text. Hence a separate header case asserting the header cells read, in order, failure class / works / fails / why.

Rejected alternatives:

- The shipped brief (`skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md`) as the home — rejected in INC-1 and not reopened: it ships to every project and binds agents at run time, while this rule binds the people who write uroboros pages.
- The table on `skills/CLAUDE.md` and on `.claude/rules/agents.md` both, so each audience carries its own copy — rejected: it breaks the one-home rule that criterion 4 names, and the two copies drift.
- A root `CLAUDE.md` as the home, or as the place to document this suite's conventions — rejected: `test-repo.sh:176` fails outright if `CLAUDE.md` exists at the repository root, because it would load as project memory and be inherited by every subagent, which no installing project reproduces.
- Keeping INC-1's line-scoped greps and adding a separate anti-inversion case — rejected: two cases per row where one cell-scoped case proves both directions, and the loose case would still read as a pass on an inverted table.
- One case looping over all four rows — rejected: criterion 5 asks for each row independently, and one case reports one failure for four different breakages.
- A new suite file — rejected: `test-repo.sh` is the home for facts about the repository itself and is already listed in `test.sh`, so a new file would need a new `test.sh` entry for nothing.

Nothing else in the repository needs to change: `test.sh` already runs `test-repo.sh`, no README or docs page enumerates `.claude/rules/`, and no shipped page gains a reference to a checkout-only file.

return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. All of them are cases appended to the existing bash suite `/home/user/uroboros/test-repo.sh`; there is no other test file and no new one.

## Framework, file and conventions

Plain bash, no framework: each case is a shell condition calling `ok "<what holds>"` or `no "<what does not>"`, both defined at the top of the file, with `$root` as the repository root. Sections open with `echo` then `echo "=== <section title>"`. Where a condition needs more than grep, the file's own style is either an inline `node -e '...' "$root"` followed by `if [ $? -eq 0 ]`, or a script written into a `mktemp -d` with a quoted heredoc and run with `node` (see the scoping case at test-repo.sh:86-121 for the second pattern). Every case carries a comment above it naming the criterion it serves and the `Break:` that would make it fail — that convention is already in the file and the new cases follow it.

All thirteen cases go in one new section, `=== a rule's form is picked by the failure it prevents`, inserted immediately before the closing `echo` / `if [ "$failed" -eq 0 ]` summary block at the end of the file.

There is no suite doc for `test-repo.sh`: the `CLAUDE.md` files under `hooks/`, `tools/*/`, `tools/*/test/` and `skills/agent-brief/assets/` document other suites, and none of them mentions this one. Do not create a repository-root `CLAUDE.md` to fill the gap — `test-repo.sh:176` fails if one exists, because it would load as inheritable project memory. If conventions need writing down, extend the header comment at the top of `test-repo.sh`; nothing in this plan requires it.

## The table parser the row cases share

Four of the cases need the table split into cells. Write one helper script — the `mktemp -d` plus quoted heredoc pattern above — taking `root`, a failure-class regex source and a JSON array of marker regex sources on argv, and run it once per row. It: reads `$root/.claude/rules/authoring.md`; takes every line whose trimmed form starts with `|`; treats the first as the header and drops any line that is only pipes, dashes, colons and spaces; splits a row on `|`, drops the empty first and last fields, trims each cell; selects the body rows whose cell 1 matches the failure-class regex, case-insensitively, and exits non-zero unless exactly one matches; then asserts every marker matches cell 2 and no marker matches cell 3, exiting non-zero with a message naming the marker and the cell that broke it. Matching is case-insensitive throughout.

## The cases

Criterion 1 — a table of exactly four rows, four named parts each.

1. Shape. Parse the table: exactly four body rows; each splits into exactly four cells; no cell is empty. Break: add a fifth row, delete one, or blank any cell — in particular the `form that fails` cell of any row.
2. Column order. The header row's cells match, in order: `failure` in cell 1, `works` in cell 2, `fails` in cell 3, `why` or `reason` in cell 4. Break: swap the `Form that works` and `Form that fails` headers — which inverts all four rows at once while every cell keeps its text, and is why this case is separate from case 1.
3. One-sentence reason. Every body row's fourth cell contains exactly one full stop, at its end (regex: one or more non-full-stop characters, then a full stop, anchored both ends). Break: split any reason cell into two sentences, or empty it.

Criterion 2 and criterion 5 — the four rows, each guarded against its own inversion. One case per row, each run of the shared parser above, each asserting the markers are all in the winning cell and none of them in the failing cell.

4. Row 1. Failure-class regex `skipped under pressure`. Markers: `prohibition`; `price` with word boundaries on both sides, so the failing form's `unpriced` cannot satisfy it; `verbatim`; `rationalisation`. Breaks, each independently red: swap cells 2 and 3 of the row (the failing form names no prohibition); replace `A prohibition` in cell 2 with `A reminder`; delete `carries its price and ` from cell 2 (criterion 6, the price); delete `, verbatim,` from cell 2 or replace `quotes, verbatim, the rationalisation it counters` with `names the rationalisation it counters` (criterion 6, the verbatim rationalisation); move any marker's wording into cell 3.
5. Row 2. Failure-class regex `output shape`. Markers: `recipe`; `output`. Breaks: swap cells 2 and 3, so the wrong output shape is paired with a list of prohibitions — the form measured to lose against it (criterion 5); replace cell 2 with `A list of prohibitions`; drop `what the output is` from cell 2.
6. Row 3. Failure-class regex `omitted required element`. Markers: `slot` with word boundaries; `schema` or `template`. Breaks: swap cells 2 and 3, so the omission is paired with prose in the body (criterion 5); replace cell 2 with `Prose in the body asking for the element`; drop `in the schema or the template` from cell 2.
7. Row 4. Failure-class regex `depends on a condition`. Marker: `observable predicate`. Breaks: swap cells 2 and 3, so the conditional behaviour is paired with a judgement call or a bolted-on exemption (criterion 5); replace `keyed to an observable predicate` in cell 2 with `left to the agent's judgement`.

Criterion 3 and criterion 6 — the exemption-clause ban.

8. The ban. Split the page on blank lines into paragraphs; in each paragraph drop every line whose trimmed form starts with `|`, then collapse the rest to one line. Take the paragraphs mentioning `exemption clause`; at least one of them must also carry `never`, `re-cut` and `observable predicate`. Stripping the table lines is load-bearing: without it, row 4's cells satisfy the assertion and the ban paragraph can be gutted while the case stays green — that is exactly the hole INC-1's second review round found. Breaks: delete the ban paragraph; replace `Never patch a working rule` with `Consider avoiding patching a working rule`; delete `Re-cut the rule` from it; replace `Re-cut the rule on an observable predicate instead` with `Re-cut the rule on your best judgement instead` (criterion 6, the observable predicate).

Criterion 4 — both audiences reached, nothing restated.

9. The home exists and is scoped to both. `.claude/rules/authoring.md` is a file, and the frontmatter between its first `---` and the next one contains both `skills/**` and `agents/**`. Break: delete the file, or drop either pattern from `paths:`. (The pre-existing scoping cases at test-repo.sh:60-121 add, for free, that the page is path-scoped at all and that both patterns match tracked files.)
10. The skill-page author is pointed at it. `skills/CLAUDE.md` contains the string `.claude/rules/authoring.md`. Break: delete the pointer sentence.
11. The agent-page author is pointed at it. `.claude/rules/agents.md` contains the string `.claude/rules/authoring.md`. Break: delete the pointer sentence.
12. One home for the ban. `grep -lie 'exemption clause'` over `agents/*.md`, `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `skills/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md`, `rulebook.md`, `README.md` and `GEMINI.md` returns exactly `$root/.claude/rules/authoring.md` and nothing else; on failure the case prints the paths it found. Break, either direction: restate the ban on a second page (two paths match), or delete it from the owner (none match). Mirror the existing `mutation_standard_owners` case at test-repo.sh:508 for the exact shell shape.
13. One home for the table. The same ownership check keyed on `rationalisation`, the table's most distinctive word. Break, either direction: restate a table row on another page, or delete row 1 from the owner.

## Deliberately not covered

Nothing beyond the criteria is tested: the page's opening prose, its citation of the measured source and its closing paragraph about its own placement carry no criterion, and pinning their wording would make every future reword a suite failure for nothing. Every one of the seven criteria has at least one case above that goes red when its behaviour is broken; criterion 7 is the command list itself.

## What counts as done

One command, run from `/home/user/uroboros`, and nothing else:

- `bash test-repo.sh`

## What is already red

I ran nothing — no suite, no probe; every fact above comes from reading. Expect `test-repo.sh` to be green at 73 cases on this branch before any change, and the thirteen new cases to fail as a block the moment they are written, since `.claude/rules/authoring.md` does not exist yet: 86 cases, 13 failing. After the page and the two pointers land, expect `PASS: 86 cases`, exit 0.

increments.title: A description names the occasion, and every shipped description is held to it
increments.goal: The authoring rules state what a description is for — the occasion to reach for the thing, never its steps — and every description this repository ships is checked against that rule and guarded by the suite, so no description can be read as a shortcut past the body it fronts and none can drift back into a summarised workflow unnoticed.
criteria: The authoring rules require a description to name the occasion for using the thing and forbid it from summarising the thing's steps, with the reason a summarised workflow becomes a shortcut agents take instead of reading the body.
That rule lives in the one home the form table and the exemption-clause ban already occupy, reaching whoever authors a skill page and whoever authors an agent page alike, and no page restates it.

Each of the four shipped skill descriptions — `agent-brief`, `argus`, `grill`, `retro` — is checked against that rule, and each one that summarises steps is rewritten so it names the occasion instead.
A rewritten skill description still leads with the words a request for that skill would actually contain, so discovery still finds it.

Each of the five agent descriptions is checked against that rule, and rewritten only where the description contradicts the body of the page it fronts; a description that merely summarises steps without contradicting its page is left as it stands.
Deleting the description rule, or dropping the occasion clause, the ban on summarising steps, or the reason from it, each turns the suite red.
For each description this increment rewrites, restoring it to the wording it replaced turns the suite red; a check that would still pass on the old wording does not satisfy this criterion.
The increment's return records the verdict for all nine descriptions by name, including the ones deliberately left unchanged and why.
